idea.title: The 132-year bottle
idea.summary: A message in a bottle thrown from a German ship in 1886 is read by a stranger on an Australian beach in 2018, closing on how quickly strangers pick up today.
hookOptions: This bottle waited 132 years for a reader
A note sat at sea for 132 years
Nobody read this note for 132 years
A stranger finally read it, 132 years late
sources: Wikipedia, Message in a bottle: oldest known message in a bottle, thrown overboard in 1886 from the German barque Paula, found in 2018 by Tonya Illman on a beach in Western Australia, after 132 years.
Western Australian Museum reports 2018: the bottle held a printed German form asking the finder to note where and when it was found and return it.

scenes.say: This bottle waited 132 years for a reader.
A German ship, the Paula, threw it overboard in 1886.
It washed up in Western Australia in 2018.
Tonya Illman spotted it on a beach.
Inside was a form asking the finder to say where.

scenes.sub: years late, but someone read it
scenes.say: The sailors were long gone. But a stranger on a beach finally read it.
That stranger took 132 years. On Random Talker, someone picks up in seconds.

Somebody threw a note into the sea in 1886 and a stranger finally read it in 2018. Would you have picked it up?
